# Primitive and pattern catalogue

Everything the Generator may put in a beat scene. Ids are exhaustive: there are no others.

An event acts on its whole target. On primitives with **part actions**, an event with `params.parts` (a list of part ids) and exactly one target acts on those parts only.

Fail → recover: a `reject` holds (red, crossed out) until a later `recover` on the same element or part ends it, with a short settle back to its own colour. Only `recover` ends a reject (`highlight`, `enter` and `pulse` do not). Every primitive and part that supports `reject` supports `recover`.

Lock → release: a `lock` holds (padlock) until a later `release` on the same element or part fades it out. Only `release` ends a lock. Every primitive and part that supports `lock` supports `release`.

## Timing, focus and transitions

- Every event plays over its action’s preset duration and easing; never set times or durations.
- A `highlight` starts about 0.2 s before its word and clears by the end of its beat or the next focus change. `params.hold: true` keeps it on (until a later `dim`, `exit` or `reject`).
- An event on several targets, a pattern instance or several parts starts them slightly apart (`enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`). `params.stagger: "scan"` makes any event a deliberate one-by-one sweep: about 0.15 s apart (parts in the element’s own order), at most 2 s and never past the beat’s next event.
- Focus: a scene’s `focus` ids show at full opacity and everything else dims (an empty `focus` dims nothing); the camera frames them. A `focus` event, valid on any element or pattern instance in scope, moves the focus to its targets from its word. While an overlay shows, focus moves to it and the board dims.
- `transitionIn` (`cut`, `fade`, `slide`, `zoom-in`, `zoom-out`) applies to a beat that starts a new board; a `continuesPrevious` beat keeps its board, so leave it at `cut`. Semantic zoom: `transitionIn: "zoom-in"` with `zoomFrom` naming an element of the previous board pushes into it, then cuts to this board (a component, then its insides).

## Primitives

### bracket

**Family:** annotation · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A curly brace that groups a run of sibling elements (`targets`), or some `parts` of one target, with a short `label` at its tip. `enter` draws the brace on, then the label fades in.

**When to use:** Naming a group: the rows that are a model’s FEATURES, the three replicas that form a QUORUM, the slots that make one BATCH.

**When not to:** A status on one element (use `tag`); an area on a map (use `zone_polygon`); a link between two elements (use `connector`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targets` | array | yes | Ids of the sibling elements the brace groups, in display order (a run next to each other). (min items 1, max items 8) |
| `parts` | array | no | Optional: group only these parts (rows, slots) of a single target. (min items 1, max items 12) |
| `label` | string | yes | Short label at the brace tip, e.g. FEATURES. (min length 1, max length 16) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Brace and label colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 372 × 90 px (min 372 × 90).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-bracket-id>",
  "primitive": "bracket",
  "props": {
    "targets": [
      "example-rows"
    ],
    "parts": [
      "example-part"
    ],
    "label": "<example-group>"
  }
}
```

### callout

**Family:** annotation · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

A small card with one or two lines of text and an optional `title`, for a counterfactual or a warning: "If the lease never expires: the lock is held forever ✗". Tinted by `semantic`: problem, focus or concept. `reject` turns it red with a cross and a shake (the assumption it states is ruled out).

**When to use:** A what-if, a caveat or a consequence that sits beside the diagram: the cost of the naive choice, a warning about a failure mode, an aside that explains a term. Set `pin` to keep it on a side of the element it belongs to.

**When not to:** A one-word status (use `tag`); a big statement over the whole scene (use `statement_card`); a number with a source (use `stat_card`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin` | object | no | Optional: pin this element to another one so it stays attached to it. |
| `title` | string | no | Optional short heading above the text, e.g. WHAT IF. (min length 1, max length 20) |
| `text` | string | yes | The counterfactual or warning; wraps to at most two lines. (min length 1, max length 64) |
| `semantic` | `problem` \| `focus` \| `concept` | no | Colour meaning: problem (a warning), focus (the point) or concept (an aside). (default `"problem"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 409 × 140 px (min 409 × 140).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-callout-id>",
  "primitive": "callout",
  "props": {
    "title": "<example-heading>",
    "text": "<example-what-if>",
    "semantic": "problem"
  }
}
```

### icon

**Family:** annotation · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A single line-drawn symbol from the asset library (server, database, user, lock, cloud), in a semantic colour, with no text.

**When to use:** A visual cue next to other elements: what kind of thing is involved, or the idea of the beat (speed, security, time) at a glance.

**When not to:** A component the story talks about (use `node_card` with an icon); an everyday object with a caption (use `item_icon`); anything that needs a word to be understood.

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asset` | string | yes | Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported). (max length 64) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Stroke colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 92 × 92 px (min 92 × 92).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-icon-id>",
  "primitive": "icon",
  "props": {
    "asset": "database",
    "semantic": "concept"
  }
}
```

### inset_panel

**Family:** annotation · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A framed detail card that zooms in over the scene while everything behind it dims. It holds other elements of the beat (`children`: e.g. a `data_block`, a `counter_transition`, a `slot_grid`, a `map_base` or a `segmented_time_bar`), drawn inside it and shown only while it is. `enter` zooms it out of its `anchor`; `exit` shrinks it back in. Children keep their own events (enter, count, highlight).

**When to use:** A closer look at one part of the diagram: what is inside a cache entry, the features a model reads for one transaction, the bins behind a warehouse pin, the time budget of one build.

**When not to:** Text only (use `statement_card` or `callout`); a whole new scene (start a new beat). Show at most one overlay at a time, and never put an overlay inside it.

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | no | Optional title in the panel header: what the detail shows. (min length 1, max length 28) |
| `anchor` | string | no | Optional id of the element the panel zooms out of (and shrinks back into). (max length 64) |
| `children` | array | yes | Ids of the elements in this beat drawn inside the panel; they show only while it does. (min items 1, max items 4) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Frame colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 860 × 900 px (min 600 × 541).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-inset_panel-id>",
  "primitive": "inset_panel",
  "props": {
    "title": "<example-detail>",
    "anchor": "example-anchor",
    "children": [
      "example-child"
    ]
  }
}
```

### item_icon

**Family:** annotation · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

A flat everyday object from the asset library (phone, car, ticket, parcel, pizza) on a soft tile, with a caption under it. `reject` turns it red with a cross and a shake.

**When to use:** The real-world thing the system is about: the parcel, the payment card, the ticket, the user's phone. Grounds an abstract flow in something the viewer has held.

**When not to:** A system component (use `node_card`); a bare symbol without a caption (use `icon`); data about the object (use `data_block`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asset` | string | yes | Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported). (max length 64) |
| `caption` | string | yes | What the object is in this story, shown under it. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Tile colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 302 × 188 px (min 302 × 188).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-item_icon-id>",
```
