### node_card

**Family:** annotation · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `lock`, `release`, `reject`, `recover`

A titled card for one component of a system (a service, server, database, client or queue), with an optional subtitle and icon. `lock` adds a padlock badge; `reject` turns it red with a cross and a shake. An optional `role` badge (a crown for the leader) sits at the top centre as the part "role": `exit` it on the old holder and `enter` it on the new one to hand the role over (a role whose first part event is `enter` starts hidden).

**When to use:** The boxes of a system diagram: anything the story treats as a component that receives, holds or sends something.

**When not to:** A label or status (use `tag`); a quantity (use `counter`); an everyday object (use `item_icon`); a bare symbol (use `icon`).

**Part actions** (events with `params.parts`): `enter`, `exit`, `pulse`

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | yes | Name of the component, shown in uppercase. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `subtitle` | string | no | Optional second line: its role or a detail. One line, at most 28 characters. (min length 1, max length 28) |
| `icon` | string | no | Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported). (max length 64) |
| `role` | string | no | Optional role badge (asset id, e.g. a crown for a leader) at the top centre. It is the part "role": exit it on the old holder and enter it on the new one to move the role. (max length 64) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Border and glow colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 573 × 138 px (min 573 × 138).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-node_card-id>",
  "primitive": "node_card",
  "props": {
    "title": "<example-name>",
    "subtitle": "<example-role>",
    "icon": "server",
    "role": "crown"
  }
}
```

### statement_card

**Family:** annotation · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

One to three large `lines` at display size on a card that spans the stage, over the dimmed scene, each line in its own colour meaning. Long lines wrap; the text never shrinks. `enter` fades it in with a slight rise. Lines are parts: `enter` a line on its word to build the statement up, highlight or pulse the one that matters. It is an overlay: everything else on the board dims while it shows.

**When to use:** A planted question ("Why not just retry forever?"), a two-line takeaway ("Easy: copy the data. Hard: keep it in sync."), a verdict before the next chapter.

**When not to:** A label next to a diagram part (use `tag` or `callout`); the beat headline (that is the HUD headline); a detail view with diagram parts in it (use `inset_panel`). Show at most one overlay at a time.

**Part actions** (events with `params.parts`): `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `pulse`

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | array | yes | One to three lines, top to bottom, each with its own colour meaning. (min items 1, max items 3) |
| `lines[].id` | string | yes | Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts. (max length 64) |
| `lines[].text` | string | yes | One large line at display size; wraps rather than shrinking. (min length 1, max length 32) |
| `lines[].semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Colour of this line: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 888 × 255 px (min 662 × 255).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-statement_card-id>",
  "primitive": "statement_card",
  "props": {
    "lines": [
      {
        "id": "easy",
        "text": "<example-easy-part>",
        "semantic": "ok"
      },
      {
        "id": "hard",
        "text": "<example-hard-part>",
        "semantic": "problem"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### tag

**Family:** annotation · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

A boxed monospace label in a semantic colour, like a sticker on the board. It names a thing, a state or a result in two or three words ("429", "CACHE HIT", "RATE LIMITED").

**When to use:** Labelling a state, outcome or status code; calling out the key term of the beat; marking a result as ok or problem. `reject` turns it red with a cross. Set `pin` to keep it on a side of the element it belongs to.

**When not to:** Sentences or explanations (the narration and headline carry those); numbers that change (use `counter`); a component or service in a system diagram.

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin` | object | no | Optional: pin this element to another one so it stays attached to it. |
| `text` | string | yes | Short label, shown in uppercase monospace. (min length 1, max length 32) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Colour meaning: neutral label, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 377 × 67 px (min 377 × 67).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-tag-id>",
  "primitive": "tag",
  "props": {
    "text": "<example-label>",
    "semantic": "problem"
  }
}
```

### command_bubble

**Family:** data · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

A speech bubble holding one line of monospace command, with the verb coloured, such as a key/value store command or a CLI call. On `enter` the command types itself out (about 30 characters a second, never more than 1.5 s). `reject` turns it red with a cross.

**When to use:** The exact request one component sends another, when the command itself teaches something: what a client asks a cache, what a producer writes to a log.

**When not to:** Data at rest (use `data_block`); several lines or real code; a plain label (use `tag`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes | The command exactly as typed, on one line. (min length 1, max length 48) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Colour of the bubble and the command verb: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"concept"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 735 × 95 px (min 735 × 95).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-command_bubble-id>",
  "primitive": "command_bubble",
  "props": {
    "text": "SET <example-key> \"<example-value>\""
  }
}
```

### data_block

**Family:** data · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A JSON-like block of key/value pairs on a card, with an optional title. On `enter` it types in one field at a time (about a third of a second each); without `enter` all fields show at once. A field can colour its value by meaning.

**When to use:** Showing what a thing looks like as data: a booking, a cache entry, a message on a queue, the record a real object becomes. Up to 6 short fields.

**When not to:** Code or logic (this is data only); a single command (use `command_bubble`); long text, nested objects or lists; a single number (use `counter`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | no | Optional name above the block, e.g. the record type. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `fields` | array | yes | The key/value pairs, in display order. (min items 1, max items 6) |
| `fields[].key` | string | yes | Field name, as it would appear in the data. |
| `fields[].value` | any | yes | Field value: a short string, a number, true/false or null. |
| `fields[].semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Colours the value and tints its row: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 733 × 258 px (min 733 × 258).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-data_block-id>",
  "primitive": "data_block",
  "props": {
    "title": "<example-record>",
    "fields": [
      {
        "key": "example_key",
        "value": "<example-value>"
      },
      {
        "key": "example_state",
        "value": "<example-state>",
        "semantic": "ok"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### formula_card

**Family:** data · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A card with one typeset formula (LaTeX, rendered by KaTeX) and an optional caption that reads it in plain words. At most 80 characters of LaTeX; invalid LaTeX is a spec error.

**When to use:** The one formula a topic genuinely rests on: attention scores, a hit ratio, the hash ring position. At most one per video, and only when the narration walks through it.

**When not to:** A single number (use `counter` or `stat_card`); an equation the narration never explains; code or data (use `data_block`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `latex` | string | yes | One formula in LaTeX math mode, without $ delimiters. Rendered by KaTeX. (min length 1, max length 80) |
| `caption` | string | no | Optional plain-words reading of the formula, shown under it. (min length 1, max length 48) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Border and glow colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"concept"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 642 × 236 px (min 642 × 236).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-formula_card-id>",
  "primitive": "formula_card",
  "props": {
    "latex": "\\text{<example-term>} = \\frac{a}{a + b}",
    "caption": "<example-reading>"
  }
}
```

### grid_overlay

**Family:** spatial · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`

A grid of square cells dropped over a map or zones. `enter` drops it in from above. The `cells` are parts addressed by row and column: `highlight` one to light it with its tag (e.g. HOT CELL), `pulse` it for attention, `reject` it to turn it red.

**When to use:** Turning space into buckets: geohash cells, a spatial index, a quadtree level, partitioning a city for drivers. Set `over` to the `map_base` it divides.

**When not to:** Irregular areas (use `zone_polygon`); a grid of items or seats (use `slot_grid`); a table of data (use `data_block`).

**Part actions** (events with `params.parts`): `highlight`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`, `dim`

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | integer | yes | Number of rows (2 to 12). (min 2, max 12) |
| `cols` | integer | yes | Number of columns (2 to 12). (min 2, max 12) |
| `over` | string | no | Optional id of the map_base or zone_polygon the grid lies over. (max length 64) |
| `cells` | array | no | Cells events can light up, by row and column. (min items 0, max items 8, default `[]`) |
| `cells[].id` | string | yes | Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts. (max length 64) |
| `cells[].row` | integer | yes | Row, counted from 1 at the top. (min 1, max 12) |
| `cells[].col` | integer | yes | Column, counted from 1 at the left. (min 1, max 12) |
| `cells[].label` | string | no | Optional tag shown when the cell lights up, e.g. HOT CELL. (min length 1, max length 14) |
| `cells[].semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Cell colour when lit: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"focus"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 880 × 880 px (min 600 × 600).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-grid_overlay-id>",
  "primitive": "grid_overlay",
  "props": {
    "rows": 6,
    "cols": 6,
    "over": "example-map",
    "cells": [
      {
        "id": "mine",
        "row": 3,
        "col": 4,
        "label": "<example-tag>"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### map_base

**Family:** spatial · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`

A stylised top-down city: blocks, streets, avenues, parks and, in the riverside `variant`, a river. A quiet background that map scenes draw on; it carries no labels. `dim` pushes it further back; `highlight` brings it forward again.

**When to use:** Any scene set in a city: ride hailing, deliveries, store coverage, nearby search. Put `route_path`, `zone_polygon` and `grid_overlay` over it.

**When not to:** Abstract systems with no geography (use `node_card` and `connector`); a world or region map; a background for its own sake.

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `downtown` \| `suburb` \| `riverside` | no | City style: downtown (dense blocks), suburb (large blocks, parks) or riverside. (default `"downtown"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 880 × 880 px (min 600 × 600).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-map_base-id>",
  "primitive": "map_base",
  "props": {
    "variant": "downtown"
  }
}
```

### radius_ring

**Family:** spatial · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A dashed search circle centred on the element `around`, with an optional `label` on its rim (the radius, or what is searched). `encloses` lists elements that must sit inside it (the circle grows to fit them). `enter` grows it out from the centre.

**When to use:** A search area or reach: couriers within 2 km of a depot, servers within one network hop, the candidates a matcher considers around a target.

**When not to:** A named area with edges (use `zone_polygon`); a grid of cells (use `grid_overlay`); a countdown (use `timer_ring`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `around` | string | yes | Id of the element in this beat at the centre of the circle. (max length 64) |
| `encloses` | array | no | Optional ids of elements the ring must enclose (the candidates in reach); it grows to fit them. (min items 1, max items 8) |
| `label` | string | no | Optional label on the ring, e.g. 2 KM. (min length 1, max length 16) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Ring colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"focus"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 520 × 550 px (min 506 × 536).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-radius_ring-id>",
  "primitive": "radius_ring",
  "props": {
    "around": "example-target",
    "encloses": [
      "example-candidate"
    ],
    "label": "<example-radius>"
  }
}
```

### route_path

**Family:** spatial · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `move`, `morph`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A glowing route through named `stops`, with a pin at the start and at the end and an optional `distance` tag. `enter` shows the pins; `move` draws the route from the first stop to the last (the tag lands when it arrives), with the optional `mover` riding its head. `mode` smooth draws a curve instead of street legs. `mode` jumpy shows raw position pings: each `move` hops the `mover` to the next stop (one `move` per stop after the first), then a `morph` draws a smooth curve through the stops and the mover glides along it. Stops are parts: highlight one, or reject it (a red cross: closed, unreachable).

**When to use:** A journey on a map: a driver to a pickup, a parcel from store to door, a packet hopping between regions. Put it over a `map_base`. Jumpy then smooth: raw GPS pings vs an interpolated track.

**When not to:** A link between two components (use `connector`); traffic over time (use `packet_stream`); areas on a map (use `zone_polygon`).

**Part actions** (events with `params.parts`): `highlight`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stops` | array | yes | Named stops in travel order, first to last. (min items 2, max items 6) |
| `stops[].id` | string | yes | Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts. (max length 64) |
| `stops[].label` | string | no | Short name of the place, e.g. a pickup point. (min length 1, max length 14) |
| `distance` | string | no | Optional distance or time tag shown at the end, e.g. 4.2 km. (min length 1, max length 12) |
| `mode` | `jumpy` \| `smooth` | no | Optional: jumpy (the mover hops stop to stop, one per move, until a morph smooths the route) or smooth (move draws a curve through the stops). Omit for street-like legs. |
| `mover` | string | no | Optional asset id of what travels the route (a bike, a car, a parcel). (max length 64) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Route colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"focus"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 840 × 620 px (min 658 × 606).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-route_path-id>",
  "primitive": "route_path",
  "props": {
    "stops": [
      {
        "id": "start",
        "label": "<example-stop>"
      },
      {
        "id": "end",
        "label": "<example-stop>"
      }
    ],
    "distance": "<example-km>",
    "mode": "jumpy",
    "mover": "bike"
  }
}
```

### zone_polygon

**Family:** spatial · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

Labelled areas drawn as soft, irregular shapes that can overlap. The `zones` are parts: `highlight` one to make it glow, `reject` to turn it red (overloaded, out of service), `dim` to push it back, `enter` to reveal it on its own word.

**When to use:** Regions on a map or coverage areas: delivery zones, cell towers, shards by region, availability zones. Put it over a `map_base`.

**When not to:** A regular grid of cells (use `grid_overlay`); components with names (use `node_card`); items in slots (use `slot_grid`).

**Part actions** (events with `params.parts`): `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zones` | array | yes | The areas, 1 to 6. (min items 1, max items 6) |
| `zones[].id` | string | yes | Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts. (max length 64) |
| `zones[].label` | string | yes | Name of the area, e.g. a delivery zone. (min length 1, max length 16) |
| `zones[].semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Zone colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"concept"`) |
| `overlap` | boolean | no | Whether neighbouring zones overlap (shared coverage) or keep a gap. (default `true`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 840 × 720 px (min 600 × 520).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-zone_polygon-id>",
  "primitive": "zone_polygon",
  "props": {
    "zones": [
      {
        "id": "zone-a",
        "label": "<example-area>"
      },
      {
        "id": "zone-b",
        "label": "<example-area>"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### connector

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `move`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

An arrow or line from one element to another, with an optional label at its middle. `enter` draws it from `from` to `to`; each `move` sends one glowing packet along it; `reject` turns it red with a cross at the middle (the link is broken or refused).

**When to use:** A relation or a hop between two elements already in the beat: a request from client to server, a write to a database, a replica link. Use `move` on the word where one thing travels.

**When not to:** Continuous traffic (add a `packet_stream` along the connector); a journey on a map (use `route_path`); a queue of waiting items (use `conveyor_queue`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | yes | Id of the element in this beat where the connector starts. (max length 64) |
| `to` | string | yes | Id of the element in this beat it points to. (max length 64) |
| `label` | string | no | Optional label at the middle: what travels, or the relation. (min length 1, max length 20) |
| `heads` | `end` \| `both` \| `none` | no | Arrowheads: end (one-way arrow), both (two-way) or none (plain line). (default `"end"`) |
| `dashed` | boolean | no | Dashed: an optional, async or planned link. (default `false`) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Line colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 347 × 84 px (min 347 × 84).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-connector-id>",
  "primitive": "connector",
  "props": {
    "from": "example-client",
    "to": "example-server",
    "label": "<example-label>"
  }
}
```

### conveyor_queue

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A horizontal belt carrying labelled blocks toward its right end, where they are taken. `items` are parts, listed in arrival order: `enter` slides one in from the left behind the others, `exit` takes it off the belt (it lifts away and the rest move up), `lock` marks it as claimed, `reject` turns it red. An item is on the belt from the start unless it first appears with `enter`.

**When to use:** Work waiting its turn: orders in a queue, jobs for a worker, messages in a partition. Take items on the words where they are processed.

**When not to:** Traffic that never waits (use `packet_stream`); items on a shelf or seats picked in any order (use `slot_grid`); a count of waiting work (use `counter`).

**Part actions** (events with `params.parts`): `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `pulse`, `lock`, `release`, `reject`, `recover`

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | yes | Blocks in arrival order: the first is at the front and is taken first. (min items 1, max items 6) |
| `items[].id` | string | yes | Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts. (max length 64) |
| `items[].label` | string | yes | Short label on the block, e.g. an order number. (min length 1, max length 7) |
| `items[].semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Block colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |
| `label` | string | no | Optional caption under the belt: what the queue is. (min length 1, max length 24) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 332 × 237 px (min 332 × 237).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-conveyor_queue-id>",
  "primitive": "conveyor_queue",
  "props": {
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "first",
        "label": "<ex-1>"
      },
      {
        "id": "second",
        "label": "<ex-2>"
      }
    ],
    "label": "<example-queue-name>"
  }
}
```

### packet_stream

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

A steady stream of small packets flowing along a `connector`, at `rate` packets per second. `enter` starts the flow from the source; `exit` stops sending (packets in flight still arrive); `reject` blocks the stream before the target: packets turn red and vanish at a barrier.

**When to use:** Ongoing traffic between two elements: requests pouring into a server, events into a queue, replication. Raise `rate` to show load growing.

**When not to:** A single request or hop (a move on the `connector` itself); items waiting in order (use `conveyor_queue`); a number of requests (use `counter`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `along` | string | yes | Id of the connector in this beat that the packets travel along. (max length 64) |
| `rate` | number | no | Packets per second (0.5 to 12). (min 0.5, max 12, default `3`) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Packet colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"concept"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 392 × 80 px (min 392 × 80).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-packet_stream-id>",
  "primitive": "packet_stream",
  "props": {
    "along": "example-connector",
    "rate": 4,
    "semantic": "concept"
  }
}
```

### counter

**Family:** metric · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `count`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

A big number with an optional unit and caption. Without a `count` event it shows `value`. With one, it shows `from` (default 0) until the count begins, then counts up or down to `value`, so the viewer watches a quantity grow or drain. With `ticking` the count runs on narration time and lands on `value` exactly at the `reject` (an outage clock that stops when the outage ends). `reject` turns the number red with a shake.

**When to use:** One quantity that matters to the story: requests per second, tokens left, queue length, latency, how long an outage lasted. Use `count` when the change itself is the point. Set `pin` to keep it on a side of the element it belongs to.

**When not to:** A word or status instead of a quantity (use `tag`); a countdown in time; several numbers at once (one counter per number, and only the ones the story needs).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin` | object | no | Optional: pin this element to another one so it stays attached to it. |
| `value` | number | yes | The number shown once any count has finished. |
| `from` | number | no | Where a `count` starts (default 0). Shown until the count begins. |
| `unit` | string | no | Short unit after the number. (min length 1, max length 16) |
| `label` | string | no | Caption under the number. (min length 1, max length 32) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Colour of the number: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"focus"`) |
| `decimals` | integer | no | Digits after the decimal point. (min 0, max 2, default `0`) |
| `ticking` | boolean | no | Count on narration time: the count runs from its word until the `reject` (else the exit or the end of the beat), like a clock. Without it a count takes under a second. (default `false`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 711 × 171 px (min 711 × 171).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-counter-id>",
  "primitive": "counter",
  "props": {
    "value": 10000,
    "from": 0,
    "unit": "<example-unit>",
    "label": "<example-caption>"
  }
}
```

### counter_transition

**Family:** metric · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `count`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A big number changing to another, shown as "10 → 9": the old number in one colour, an arrow, the new number in another. Without a `count` event it shows the change as done. With one, the old number stands alone until the count, then the arrow and the new number come in and the old one fades back. A null `from` shows "?": an unknown value revealed as a prediction or a measured result ("? → 0.82").

**When to use:** One discrete change the story turns on: 10 free lockers dropping to 9, a version going from 1 to 2, a retry count ticking up. The colour change carries the meaning (e.g. neutral to problem). With `from` null: a prediction appearing, an unknown measured for the first time.

**When not to:** A quantity that counts smoothly up or down (use `counter`); a countdown in time; more than one change at once.

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | number,null | yes | The number before the change, or null when it is unknown (shown as "?"). |
| `to` | number | yes | The number after the change. |
| `unit` | string | no | Short unit after the new number. (min length 1, max length 16) |
| `label` | string | no | Caption under the numbers. (min length 1, max length 32) |
| `fromSemantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Colour of the old number: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |
| `toSemantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Colour of the new number: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"focus"`) |
| `decimals` | integer | no | Digits after the decimal point. (min 0, max 2, default `0`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 759 × 134 px (min 759 × 134).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-counter_transition-id>",
  "primitive": "counter_transition",
  "props": {
    "from": 10,
    "to": 9,
    "unit": "<example-unit>",
    "fromSemantic": "ok",
    "toSemantic": "problem"
  }
}
```

### segmented_time_bar

**Family:** metric · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A stacked bar splitting a time budget into steps (BUILD | TEST), each segment as wide as its time with its mm:ss under it, and the total at the top right. With `budgetSec`, a marker shows the budget and any time past it turns red. `enter` fills the segments left to right; segments are parts: highlight the step being discussed, reject the one that blows the budget.

**When to use:** Where time goes in a flow: a 10-minute delivery promise, the latency budget of a request, the stages of a deploy. Use it when the split matters more than one number.

**When not to:** A single countdown (use `timer_ring`); one number (use `counter` or `stat_card`); steps without durations (use `node_card` and `connector`).

**Part actions** (events with `params.parts`): `highlight`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`, `dim`

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `segments` | array | yes | Steps in order, left to right (1 to 5). (min items 1, max items 5) |
| `segments[].id` | string | yes | Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts. (max length 64) |
| `segments[].label` | string | yes | Short name of the step, e.g. BUILD or TEST. (min length 1, max length 8) |
| `segments[].sec` | integer | yes | How long the step takes, in seconds. (min 1, max 5999) |
| `segments[].semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Segment colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"concept"`) |
| `budgetSec` | integer | no | Optional time budget: a marker on the bar; time past it is drawn red. (min 1, max 5999) |
| `label` | string | no | Optional caption: what the time is for, e.g. COMMIT TO DEPLOY. (min length 1, max length 24) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 840 × 187 px (min 310 × 187).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-segmented_time_bar-id>",
  "primitive": "segmented_time_bar",
  "props": {
    "segments": [
      {
        "id": "step-a",
        "label": "<ex-a>",
        "sec": 90
      },
      {
        "id": "step-b",
        "label": "<ex-b>",
        "sec": 120
      }
    ],
    "budgetSec": 600
  }
}
```

### stat_card

**Family:** metric · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A card with one big figure, a label under it, and a small source footnote. The figure is text, so units and formatting stay as written ("10k/s", "₹2,000 Cr", "99.9%").

**When to use:** A cited real-world number that makes the problem concrete: traffic at peak, money lost, a benchmark. Every figure from research needs its source.

**When not to:** A number that animates or changes (use `counter` or `counter_transition`); an illustrative number with no source (use `counter`); a label or status (use `tag`).

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | yes | The figure as displayed, units included. (min length 1, max length 12) |
| `label` | string | yes | What the figure measures. (min length 1, max length 32) |
| `source` | string | yes | Where the figure comes from, shown as a footnote. Required. (min length 1, max length 60) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Colour of the value: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"focus"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 815 × 245 px (min 815 × 245).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-stat_card-id>",
  "primitive": "stat_card",
  "props": {
    "value": "<example-n>",
    "label": "<example-label>",
    "source": "<example-source>"
  }
}
```

### timer_ring

**Family:** metric · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `count`, `reject`, `recover`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A countdown ring with the time left as mm:ss in the middle. It shows `durationSec` until `count` starts the clock. Its pace is set by the narration: it reaches 00:00 exactly on the `reject` (expiry: empty ring, red flash); without `reject` it runs out at the element's `exit` or the end of the beat, and holds 00:00. It never runs slower than real time; when faster, a fast-forward tag shows the multiplier (e.g. 60×).

**When to use:** A deadline or hold in the story: a room held for 10 minutes, a token that expires, a lease or a timeout. Put `count` where the clock starts and `reject` on the word where the time runs out. Set `pin` to keep it on a side of the element it belongs to.

**When not to:** A quantity that is not time (use `counter`); elapsed time across the whole video (that is the story clock in the HUD); a duration that never runs down.

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin` | object | no | Optional: pin this element to another one so it stays attached to it. |
| `durationSec` | integer | yes | Time on the clock when it starts, in seconds (600 shows 10:00). (min 1, max 5999) |
| `label` | string | no | Caption under the ring: what the time is for. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Ring colour while running: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"focus"`) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 302 × 290 px (min 302 × 290).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-timer_ring-id>",
  "primitive": "timer_ring",
  "props": {
    "durationSec": 600,
    "label": "<example-caption>"
  }
}
```

### device_frame

**Family:** object · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`, `morph`

A generic phone or tablet outline (`kind`) with a simple screen: a `status` line, list `rows`, and a `button`. `morph` changes the button to its "then" label and colour (Claim → Claimed ✓). Rows are parts: enter one as it arrives, highlight it, or reject it (red with a cross: declined, failed). Never a real app, screenshot or logo.

**When to use:** What a user sees: an incoming task, a request to approve, a list of notifications, the status of a payment.

**When not to:** A server or service (use `node_card`); a phone as an everyday object without a screen (use `item_icon`); data fields (use `data_block`).

**Part actions** (events with `params.parts`): `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `pulse`, `reject`, `recover`

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `phone` \| `tablet` | no | Outline: phone (tall) or tablet. (default `"phone"`) |
| `status` | string | no | Optional status line at the top of the screen. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `rows` | array | no | Optional list rows, top to bottom. (min items 1, max items 5) |
| `rows[].id` | string | yes | Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts. (max length 64) |
| `rows[].label` | string | yes | Row text: a task, a contact, a message. (min length 1, max length 22) |
| `rows[].detail` | string | no | Optional short value at the right, e.g. 3 MIN. (min length 1, max length 12) |
| `rows[].icon` | string | no | Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported). (max length 64) |
| `button` | object | no |  |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 549 × 808 px (min 549 × 808).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-device_frame-id>",
  "primitive": "device_frame",
  "props": {
    "status": "<example-status>",
    "rows": [
      {
        "id": "example-row",
        "label": "<example-row>",
        "detail": "<example-v>"
      }
    ],
    "button": {
      "label": "<example-action>",
      "then": {
        "label": "<example-done>",
        "semantic": "ok"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### slot_grid

**Family:** object · **Actions:** `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`

A grid of labelled slots: bins of stock, a shelf, cinema seats or documents. Each slot is a part: `lock` claims it (padlock, yellow), `highlight` picks it out, `exit` takes its item (it lifts away and leaves an empty outline), `enter` puts an item back, `reject` turns it red with a cross (sold out, conflict).

**When to use:** Contention over specific items: two users grabbing the same locker, stock picked from bins, which documents a search touches. Address the slots on the words that act on them.

**When not to:** Items moving in order (use `conveyor_queue`); a spatial grid over a map (use `grid_overlay`); one standalone object (use `item_icon`).

**Part actions** (events with `params.parts`): `enter`, `exit`, `lock`, `release`, `highlight`, `reject`, `recover`, `pulse`, `dim`

**Props:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `inventory` \| `shelf` \| `seats` \| `documents` | no | How slots look: inventory (bins), shelf (rows on planks), seats, documents. (default `"inventory"`) |
| `slots` | array | yes | The slots, in reading order (1 to 24). (min items 1, max items 24) |
| `slots[].id` | string | yes | Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts. (max length 64) |
| `slots[].label` | string | yes | Short label on the slot, e.g. a slot number or an item name. (min length 1, max length 7) |
| `slots[].icon` | string | no | Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported). (max length 64) |
| `slots[].semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Slot colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. (default `"neutral"`) |
| `cols` | integer | no | Slots per row; omit to choose from the slot count. (min 1, max 6) |
| `label` | string | no | Optional caption under the grid. (min length 1, max length 24) |

**Size hint** (example, drafting-paper): 414 × 111.6 px (min 414 × 111.6).

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-slot_grid-id>",
  "primitive": "slot_grid",
  "props": {
    "kind": "seats",
    "slots": [
      {
        "id": "seat-1",
        "label": "<ex-1>"
      },
      {
        "id": "seat-2",
        "label": "<ex-2>"
      },
      {
        "id": "seat-3",
        "label": "<ex-3>"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Patterns

A pattern is a reusable piece of choreography: it expands into primitives and timed events, anchored to the narration words in `params.at`. It stages its own entrances. Events on the instance may use only its **Actions**; events on one element inside it, targeted as `<instance>/<id>`, may use only `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`. A beat without its own `layoutMode` uses its patterns' layout mode.

### versus_split

**Family:** annotation · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

Two halves side by side get the same event at the same moment, and each shows its own outcome: the side that handles it lights up with its verdict, the side that fails turns red.

**When to use:** Comparing two designs under one condition: SQL vs NoSQL under a write burst, sync vs async on a slow call, temperature 0 vs 1 on one prompt.

**When not to:** A near and a far store (use `cache_hit_miss`); a slow way then a fast way in sequence (use `brute_force_then_index`).

**Layout mode:** `versus_split`

**Formats:** `full`, `card`

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `show`: Both sides appear.
- `event`: The same event reaches both sides at once.
- `verdict`: Each side shows how it handled it.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `event`: The shared event tag.
- `left`: The left side.
- `right`: The right side.
- `left-link`: Arrow from the event to the left side.
- `right-link`: Arrow from the event to the right side.
- `left-verdict`: The verdict tag on the left.
- `right-verdict`: The verdict tag on the right.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | string | yes | The one event both sides get, as a short tag, e.g. 10K WRITES. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `left` | object | yes | The left side. |
| `right` | object | yes | The right side. |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-versus_split-id>",
  "pattern": "versus_split",
  "params": {
    "event": "<example-event>",
    "left": {
      "title": "<example-left>",
      "verdict": "<example-verdict>",
      "outcome": "ok"
    },
    "right": {
      "title": "<example-right>",
      "verdict": "<example-verdict>",
      "outcome": "problem"
    },
    "at": {
      "show": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "event": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "verdict": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### brute_force_then_index

**Family:** data · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A brute-force search sweeps the items one by one and each turns red (the target pulses as the sweep passes it), with a tag naming the cost. Then an index appears and jumps straight to the one item, which lights up.

**When to use:** Brute force before the clever fix: a full table scan vs an index, checking every zone vs a grid cell lookup, a linear search vs a hash map.

**When not to:** A fast and a slow store side by side (use `cache_hit_miss`); two whole designs compared (use `versus_split`).

**Layout mode:** `centered_focus`

**Formats:** `full`, `card` (`full` only with more than 4 items)

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `scan`: Every item is checked one by one and turns red.
- `slow`: The cost of checking everything is named.
- `index`: The index appears.
- `found`: The index jumps straight to the right item.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `items`: The items, a slot grid; its slots are parts item-1, item-2, …
- `cost`: The brute-force cost tag.
- `index`: The index.
- `jump`: Arrow from the index to the items.
- `fast`: The indexed cost tag.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | yes | The items a brute-force search checks, 4 to 12, in reading order. (min items 4, max items 12) |
| `kind` | `inventory` \| `shelf` \| `seats` \| `documents` | no | How items look: inventory, shelf, seats or documents. (default `"documents"`) |
| `target` | string | yes | Label of the item being looked for; one of items. (min length 1, max length 7) |
| `cost` | string | no | Tag naming the brute-force cost. (min length 1, max length 24, default `"CHECK ALL = SLOW"`) |
| `index` | object | yes | The index or lookup structure (a hash map, a B-tree, a grid). |
| `fast` | string | no | Tag naming the indexed cost. (min length 1, max length 24, default `"ONE LOOKUP"`) |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-brute_force_then_index-id>",
  "pattern": "brute_force_then_index",
  "params": {
    "items": [
      "<ex-1>",
      "<ex-2>",
      "<ex-3>",
      "<ex-4>"
    ],
    "target": "<ex-3>",
    "index": {
      "title": "<example-index>",
      "icon": "key"
    },
    "at": {
      "scan": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "slow": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "index": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      },
      "found": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 3
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### inference_card

**Family:** data · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

Inputs → model → prediction. Feature rows type in, grouped by a bracket, and flow into a model; the prediction flips from "?" to a value. An optional comparison feeds a second input with a different value in and gets a different prediction.

**When to use:** Any ML prediction told as data in, number out: fraud score, delivery ETA, churn risk, price. Use the comparison to show which feature changes the answer.

**When not to:** A single number without inputs (use `counter_transition`); a decision between candidates (use `pick_by_rule`).

**Layout mode:** `pipeline`

**Formats:** `full`

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `inputs`: The feature rows type in and are grouped.
- `model`: The features flow into the model.
- `predict`: The prediction flips from "?" to its value.
- `compare` (optional): A second input and its different prediction (only with comparison).

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `features`: The feature rows.
- `group`: The bracket around the features.
- `model`: The model.
- `in-link`: Arrow from the features to the model.
- `out-link`: Arrow from the model to the prediction.
- `prediction`: The prediction ("?" until predict).
- `compare-features`: The second input (with comparison).
- `compare-link`: Arrow from the second input to the model.
- `compare-prediction`: The second prediction.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | no | Optional title of the input record, e.g. ORDER 4127. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `features` | array | yes | The input features as key/value rows, 1 to 5. (min items 1, max items 5) |
| `features[].key` | string | yes | Field name, as it would appear in the data. |
| `features[].value` | any | yes | Field value: a short string, a number, true/false or null. |
| `features[].semantic` | `neutral` \| `focus` \| `ok` \| `problem` \| `concept` | no | Colours the value and tints its row: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept. |
| `group` | string | no | Label of the bracket around the features. (min length 1, max length 16, default `"FEATURES"`) |
| `model` | object | yes | The model that reads the features. |
| `prediction` | object | yes | What the model predicts for these features. |
| `comparison` | object | no | Optional second input with a different result; needs at.compare. |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-inference_card-id>",
  "pattern": "inference_card",
  "params": {
    "features": [
      {
        "key": "example_feature",
        "value": "<example-value>"
      },
      {
        "key": "example_count",
        "value": 3
      }
    ],
    "model": {
      "title": "<example-model>",
      "icon": "cpu"
    },
    "prediction": {
      "value": 14,
      "unit": "<example-unit>"
    },
    "comparison": {
      "features": [
        {
          "key": "example_feature",
          "value": "<example-other>"
        }
      ],
      "prediction": {
        "value": 22,
        "unit": "<example-unit>"
      }
    },
    "at": {
      "inputs": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "model": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "predict": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      },
      "compare": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 3
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### pick_by_rule

**Family:** spatial · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

Candidates around a target, optionally inside a search ring that encloses them. The obvious pick (nearest, first, cheapest) gets a tag and is crossed out; the right one is ringed, linked to the target and tagged with the rule that makes it win ("FREE + 12 MS").

**When to use:** Matching and scheduling decisions where the naive rule is wrong: couriers to parcels, servers to requests, cache nodes to keys, workers to jobs.

**When not to:** A prediction from features (use `inference_card`); two designs compared (use `versus_split`).

**Layout mode:** `hub_spoke`

**Formats:** `full`

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `show`: The target and the candidates around it appear.
- `obvious`: The obvious pick is named (nearest, first, cheapest).
- `cross`: The obvious pick is crossed out.
- `pick`: The right pick is ringed with the reason it wins.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `target`: The target.
- `ring`: The search ring (with radius).
- `candidate-<id>`: The candidate with that id.
- `obvious-tag`: The tag on the obvious pick.
- `pick-tag`: The reason tag on the right pick.
- `pick-link`: Arrow from the right pick to the target.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | object | yes | What is being matched (an order, a request, a key). |
| `radius` | string | no | Optional label of a search ring around the target, e.g. 2 KM. (min length 1, max length 16) |
| `candidates` | array | yes | The candidates around the target, 3 to 5. (min items 3, max items 5) |
| `candidates[].id` | string | yes | Short slug for this candidate, used by obvious and pick. (max length 64) |
| `candidates[].title` | string | yes | Name of the candidate, e.g. SERVER 2. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `candidates[].detail` | string | no | Optional detail under the name, e.g. 12 MS AWAY. (min length 1, max length 28) |
| `candidates[].icon` | string | no | Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported). (max length 64) |
| `obvious` | object | yes | The tempting pick that is wrong. |
| `pick` | object | yes | The pick the rule chooses, with its reason. |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-pick_by_rule-id>",
  "pattern": "pick_by_rule",
  "params": {
    "target": {
      "title": "<example-target>",
      "icon": "package"
    },
    "radius": "<example-km>",
    "candidates": [
      {
        "id": "example-a",
        "title": "<example-a>",
        "detail": "<example-detail>"
      },
      {
        "id": "example-b",
        "title": "<example-b>"
      },
      {
        "id": "example-c",
        "title": "<example-c>"
      }
    ],
    "obvious": {
      "candidate": "example-a",
      "reason": "<example-nearest>"
    },
    "pick": {
      "candidate": "example-b",
      "reason": "<example-reason>"
    },
    "at": {
      "show": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "obvious": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "cross": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      },
      "pick": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 3
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### atomic_lock

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

Two requests race for one resource. The first arrives and locks it (padlock) and a hold timer starts; the second arrives while it is held, its arrow turns red and it is tagged with a cross. With a `release` anchor, the hold timer runs out there and the resource is released.

**When to use:** Contention for one thing: two users booking the same room, two workers claiming the same job, two writers on one row. The moment the lock makes the second attempt fail.

**When not to:** Rejecting a repeat of the same request (use `reject_duplicate`); many requests overwhelming a server (use `flood_then_funnel`).

**Layout mode:** `hub_spoke`

**Formats:** `full`

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `arrive`: The first request reaches the resource.
- `lock`: The resource is locked and the hold timer starts.
- `second`: A second request arrives for the same resource.
- `bounce`: The second request is turned away.
- `release` (optional): The hold ends: the timer runs out and the resource is free again. Leave it out to keep the lock held to the end of the beat.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `resource`: The locked resource.
- `first`: The request that holds the lock.
- `second`: The request that bounces.
- `first-link`: Arrow from the first request to the resource.
- `second-link`: Arrow from the second request (rejected on bounce).
- `hold`: The hold timer (it exits when the hold ends).
- `bounced`: The tag on the turned-away request.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | object | yes | The one thing both requests want (a room, a row, a slot). |
| `first` | object | yes | The request that gets there first. |
| `second` | object | yes | The request that arrives while the lock is held. |
| `holdSec` | integer | yes | How long the lock holds, in seconds (the hold timer starts here). (min 1, max 5999) |
| `holdLabel` | string | no | Optional caption under the hold timer. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `bounce` | string | no | Tag on the turned-away request, e.g. ALREADY HELD. (min length 1, max length 24, default `"LOCKED"`) |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-atomic_lock-id>",
  "pattern": "atomic_lock",
  "params": {
    "resource": {
      "title": "<example-resource>",
      "icon": "lock"
    },
    "first": {
      "title": "<example-first>",
      "icon": "user"
    },
    "second": {
      "title": "<example-second>",
      "icon": "user"
    },
    "holdSec": 600,
    "holdLabel": "<example-hold>",
    "bounce": "<example-bounce>",
    "at": {
      "arrive": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "lock": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "second": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      },
      "bounce": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 3
      },
      "release": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 4
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### cache_hit_miss

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A client with a near store and a far store. A hit is answered by the near store and tagged with its small latency; a miss goes on to the far store and is tagged with its large one, so the gap in latency is the lesson.

**When to use:** Caching, CDNs and any near/far trade-off: cache vs database, edge vs origin, memory vs disk, KV cache vs recomputation.

**When not to:** Comparing two whole designs side by side (use `versus_split`); a flood of requests on one node (use `flood_then_funnel`).

**Layout mode:** `near_far`

**Formats:** `full`

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `show`: The client, the near store and the far store appear.
- `hit`: A request is answered by the near store (fast).
- `miss`: A request misses the near store and goes on to the far one (slow).

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `client`: The client.
- `near`: The near store.
- `far`: The far store.
- `near-link`: Arrow from the client to the near store.
- `far-link`: Arrow from the near store to the far store (the miss path).
- `hit`: The HIT tag with its latency.
- `miss`: The MISS tag with its latency.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `client` | object | yes | Who asks (a user, an app server). |
| `near` | object | yes | The near, fast store (a cache, an edge server). |
| `far` | object | yes | The far, slow store (a database, the origin). |
| `hitLatency` | string | yes | Latency of a hit, e.g. 2 ms. (min length 1, max length 12) |
| `missLatency` | string | yes | Latency of a miss, e.g. 2 ms. (min length 1, max length 12) |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-cache_hit_miss-id>",
  "pattern": "cache_hit_miss",
  "params": {
    "client": {
      "title": "<example-client>",
      "icon": "user"
    },
    "near": {
      "title": "<example-near>",
      "icon": "zap"
    },
    "far": {
      "title": "<example-far>",
      "icon": "database"
    },
    "hitLatency": "<example-ms>",
    "missLatency": "<example-ms>",
    "at": {
      "show": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "hit": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "miss": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### converge_adapter

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

Two to four inputs, each drawn in a different style, flow into a hub; one output in a single, uniform style comes out. The visual point is many shapes in, one shape out.

**When to use:** Adapters and normalisation: payment providers behind one gateway, log formats into one schema, model providers behind one client.

**When not to:** One message copied out to many (use `fan_out`); a flood of identical requests (use `flood_then_funnel`).

**Layout mode:** `pipeline`

**Formats:** `full`, `card`

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `inputs`: The differently shaped inputs appear.
- `convert`: The hub appears and each input flows into it.
- `output`: One uniform output leaves the hub.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `input-<n>`: The n-th input (from 1).
- `link-<n>`: Arrow from the n-th input into the hub.
- `hub`: The adapter hub.
- `out-link`: Arrow from the hub to the output.
- `output`: The uniform output.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inputs` | array | yes | The inputs, 2 to 4; each is drawn in a different style. (min items 2, max items 4) |
| `hub` | object | yes | The adapter or gateway that normalises them. |
| `output` | string | yes | The one uniform output, e.g. ORDER EVENT. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-converge_adapter-id>",
  "pattern": "converge_adapter",
  "params": {
    "inputs": [
      "<example-input-1>",
      "<example-input-2>",
      "<example-input-3>"
    ],
    "hub": {
      "title": "<example-hub>",
      "icon": "layers"
    },
    "output": "<example-output>",
    "at": {
      "inputs": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "convert": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "output": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### failover

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A writer, a leader with the role badge and its followers. The leader fails: it turns red and its links break. The badge leaves the old leader and appears on the first follower, then the writer and the other followers re-link to the new leader.

**When to use:** Leader election and failover: a database primary dying, a broker partition leader moving, a lock holder replaced. The concept beat before a real incident.

**When not to:** Both sides believing they lead after a network split (use `split_brain`); one request refused while a lock is held (use `atomic_lock`).

**Layout mode:** `pipeline`

**Formats:** `full`, `card`

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `steady`: Writes reach the leader and replicate to the followers.
- `fail`: The leader fails and its links break.
- `promote`: The role moves from the old leader to the first follower.
- `reroute`: The writer and the other followers link to the new leader.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `writer`: The writer.
- `leader`: The old leader.
- `follower-<n>`: The n-th follower (from 1); follower-1 is promoted.
- `write`: Arrow from the writer to the old leader.
- `repl-<n>`: Replication arrow from the old leader to the n-th follower.
- `new-write`: Arrow from the writer to the new leader.
- `new-repl-<n>`: Replication arrow from the new leader to the n-th follower.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `writer` | object | yes | Who writes (an app server, a client). |
| `leader` | object | yes | The leader that fails. |
| `followers` | array | yes | The followers, 1 to 3; the first one is promoted. (min items 1, max items 3) |
| `followers[].title` | string | yes | Name of the component, shown in uppercase. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `followers[].icon` | string | no | Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported). (max length 64) |
| `role` | string | no | Asset id of the role badge (a crown). (max length 64, default `"crown"`) |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-failover-id>",
  "pattern": "failover",
  "params": {
    "writer": {
      "title": "<example-writer>",
      "icon": "server"
    },
    "leader": {
      "title": "<example-leader>",
      "icon": "database"
    },
    "followers": [
      {
        "title": "<example-follower-1>",
        "icon": "database"
      },
      {
        "title": "<example-follower-2>",
        "icon": "database"
      }
    ],
    "at": {
      "steady": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "fail": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "promote": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      },
      "reroute": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 3
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### fan_out

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

One message leaves a source and splits into a copy per target (a packet on each arrow), then the targets pass it on to a crowd whose count climbs.

**When to use:** Fan-out and pub/sub: one post reaching every follower, one event delivered to several services, a broadcast through regional servers.

**When not to:** Many inputs merging into one (use `converge_adapter`); work shared out from a queue (use `worker_pool`).

**Layout mode:** `pipeline`

**Formats:** `full`, `card` (`full` only with more than 2 targets)

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `send`: The source sends the one message.
- `split`: The message is copied to every target.
- `crowd`: The copies reach the crowd behind the targets.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `source`: The source.
- `message`: The message tag at the source.
- `target-<n>`: The n-th target (from 1).
- `link-<n>`: Arrow from the source to the n-th target.
- `reach-<n>`: Arrow from the n-th target to the crowd.
- `crowd`: The crowd counter.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | object | yes | Where the message starts (a publisher, a post, a broker). |
| `message` | string | yes | The message, as a short tag, e.g. NEW POST. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `targets` | array | yes | The targets the message splits to, 2 to 4. (min items 2, max items 4) |
| `targets[].title` | string | yes | Name of the component, shown in uppercase. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `targets[].icon` | string | no | Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported). (max length 64) |
| `crowd` | object | yes | The crowd the targets deliver to, counted up as copies reach it. |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-fan_out-id>",
  "pattern": "fan_out",
  "params": {
    "source": {
      "title": "<example-source>",
      "icon": "mail"
    },
    "message": "<example-message>",
    "targets": [
      {
        "title": "<example-target-1>"
      },
      {
        "title": "<example-target-2>"
      }
    ],
    "crowd": {
      "value": 100000,
      "label": "<example-crowd>"
    },
    "at": {
      "send": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "split": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "crowd": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### flood_then_funnel

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A dense stream of requests hits a node directly while the rate counts up; the node shakes red and a warning shows. Then a middle layer steps in: the flood goes into it and a single, slow, steady line comes out to the node, which recovers.

**When to use:** Failure before the fix for load: a rate limiter, a queue, a cache or a CDN absorbing a spike that would knock a server over.

**When not to:** Two requests for one resource (use `atomic_lock`); one message copied to many targets (use `fan_out`).

**Layout mode:** `pipeline`

**Formats:** `full`

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `flood`: The flood of requests starts and the rate counts up.
- `overwhelm`: The target gives way: it shakes red and a warning shows.
- `funnel`: The middle layer appears, turns the flood into one steady line, and the target recovers.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `source`: Where the flood comes from.
- `target`: The overwhelmed node.
- `layer`: The middle layer (enters on the funnel).
- `direct`: The direct arrow from source to target (exits on the funnel).
- `flood`: The dense packet stream on the direct arrow.
- `rate`: The flood rate counter.
- `warning`: The warning tag on the target.
- `in`: Arrow from the source into the layer.
- `in-flow`: The dense stream into the layer.
- `out`: Arrow from the layer to the target.
- `out-flow`: The single steady stream out of the layer.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | object | yes | Where the flood comes from (clients, users, producers). |
| `target` | object | yes | The node that is overwhelmed (an API, a database). |
| `layer` | object | yes | The middle layer that absorbs the flood (a queue, a rate limiter, a CDN). |
| `rate` | object | yes | The flood rate, counted up from 0 as the flood starts. |
| `warning` | string | no | Tag shown when the target gives way. (min length 1, max length 24, default `"OVERLOADED"`) |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-flood_then_funnel-id>",
  "pattern": "flood_then_funnel",
  "params": {
    "source": {
      "title": "<example-source>",
      "icon": "users"
    },
    "target": {
      "title": "<example-target>",
      "icon": "server"
    },
    "layer": {
      "title": "<example-layer>",
      "icon": "layers"
    },
    "rate": {
      "value": 10000,
      "unit": "<example-unit>"
    },
    "at": {
      "flood": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "overwhelm": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "funnel": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### reject_duplicate

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

The same request arrives twice. The first copy travels to the receiver and is accepted; the second, carrying the same id, is turned red and stamped DUPLICATE, so the work happens once.

**When to use:** Idempotency and deduplication: a payment retried after a timeout, a message delivered twice, a double-clicked submit.

**When not to:** Two different requests competing for one resource (use `atomic_lock`); a request that fails for another reason (use a `tag` or `callout`).

**Layout mode:** `pipeline`

**Formats:** `full`

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `first`: The request arrives the first time and is processed.
- `second`: The same request (same id) arrives again.
- `stamp`: The repeat is recognised and stamped as a duplicate.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `sender`: The sender.
- `receiver`: The receiver that dedupes.
- `link`: Arrow from sender to receiver; a packet travels on each arrival.
- `first`: The first copy of the id (accepted).
- `second`: The second copy (rejected).
- `duplicate`: The stamp on the second copy.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sender` | object | yes | Who sends the request (a client retrying, a producer). |
| `receiver` | object | yes | Who checks the id and processes the request once. |
| `key` | string | yes | The id both copies carry, as shown, e.g. order_id 7781. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `stamp` | string | no | Stamp on the repeat. (min length 1, max length 16, default `"DUPLICATE"`) |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-reject_duplicate-id>",
  "pattern": "reject_duplicate",
  "params": {
    "sender": {
      "title": "<example-sender>",
      "icon": "smartphone"
    },
    "receiver": {
      "title": "<example-receiver>",
      "icon": "server"
    },
    "key": "<example-key>",
    "at": {
      "first": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "second": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "stamp": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### split_brain

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

Two regions with a leader and a replica. The link breaks (red, then dashed) and an outage clock counts up; cut off, the replica takes the role badge too. Each side accepts a different write. When the link returns the clock stops, both nodes hold the badge and a conflict callout names the damage.

**When to use:** Network partitions and split brain: two primaries after a partition, fencing and leases, why quorums exist; the real-incident beat after a `failover` concept beat.

**When not to:** A clean failover where the old leader is really gone (use `failover`); a single request refused under a lock (use `atomic_lock`).

**Layout mode:** `versus_split`

**Formats:** `full`, `card` (`full` only with the lease timer)

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `steady`: The leader replicates to the far replica over the link.
- `partition`: The link between the regions breaks; the outage clock starts.
- `promote`: The far replica, cut off, takes the role badge too.
- `writes`: Each side accepts a different write.
- `heal`: The link returns: the clock stops and the conflict shows.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `leader`: The leader.
- `replica`: The far replica.
- `link`: The replication link (rejected on partition).
- `cut`: The dashed, broken link during the partition.
- `restored`: The link after the heal.
- `outage`: The outage clock (counts up, red when it stops).
- `lease`: The optional lease timer.
- `leader-write`: The leader's write.
- `replica-write`: The replica's write.
- `conflict`: The conflict callout.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `leader` | object | yes | The leader in the first region. |
| `replica` | object | yes | The replica in the far region that promotes itself. |
| `role` | string | no | Asset id of the role badge (a crown). (max length 64, default `"crown"`) |
| `outage` | object | yes | The outage clock: counts up from the partition and stops on the heal. |
| `lease` | object | no | Optional lease timer that runs out when the replica promotes itself. |
| `writes` | object | yes | The divergent writes, one per side. |
| `conflict` | string | yes | The conflict, stated plainly, e.g. Two owners for one record. (min length 1, max length 64) |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-split_brain-id>",
  "pattern": "split_brain",
  "params": {
    "leader": {
      "title": "<example-leader>",
      "icon": "database"
    },
    "replica": {
      "title": "<example-replica>",
      "icon": "database"
    },
    "outage": {
      "sec": 43
    },
    "lease": {
      "durationSec": 10
    },
    "writes": {
      "leader": "<example-write-a>",
      "replica": "<example-write-b>"
    },
    "conflict": "<example-conflict>",
    "at": {
      "steady": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "partition": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "promote": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      },
      "writes": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 3
      },
      "heal": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 4
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### worker_pool

**Family:** flow · **Actions:** `exit`, `highlight`, `dim`, `pulse`

A queue of waiting jobs feeds a pool of workers: on the assign word each worker takes the job at the front (the jobs lift off the belt) and works on it, then each produces an output.

**When to use:** Background jobs, consumers on a queue, thread pools, parallel inference: work waiting its turn and shared out across several workers.

**When not to:** One message copied to every target (use `fan_out`); a single queue with no workers (use a `conveyor_queue`).

**Layout mode:** `pipeline`

**Formats:** `full`, `card` (`full` only with more than 2 workers)

**Narration anchors** (`params.at`):

- `queue`: The queue of waiting jobs and the idle workers appear.
- `assign`: Each worker takes the job at the front of the queue.
- `done`: Each worker produces its output.

**Inner elements** (target as `<instance>/<id>` with `highlight`, `pulse`, `dim`):

- `queue`: The job queue; its jobs are parts job-1, job-2, …
- `worker-<n>`: The n-th worker (from 1).
- `link-<n>`: Arrow from the queue to the n-th worker.
- `output-<n>`: The output of the n-th worker.

**Params:**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `queue` | string | no | Optional caption under the queue, e.g. JOB QUEUE. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `jobs` | array | yes | Waiting jobs in arrival order, 2 to 6; the first is at the front. (min items 2, max items 6) |
| `workers` | array | yes | The workers, 2 to 4 (at most one per job). (min items 2, max items 4) |
| `workers[].title` | string | yes | Name of the component, shown in uppercase. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `workers[].icon` | string | no | Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported). (max length 64) |
| `output` | string | yes | What each worker produces, e.g. THUMBNAIL. (min length 1, max length 24) |
| `at` | object | yes | Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment. |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "id": "<example-worker_pool-id>",
  "pattern": "worker_pool",
  "params": {
    "queue": "<example-queue>",
    "jobs": [
      "<ex-1>",
      "<ex-2>",
      "<ex-3>"
    ],
    "workers": [
      {
        "title": "<example-worker-1>"
      },
      {
        "title": "<example-worker-2>"
      }
    ],
    "output": "<example-output>",
    "at": {
      "queue": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 0
      },
      "assign": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 1
      },
      "done": {
        "type": "word",
        "index": 2
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Layout modes

Ids are exhaustive. Elements may name a zone of their beat’s layout mode.

| Mode | Zones | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `map` | `base`, `overlay`, `marker`, `aside` | A map base filling the stage, overlays sharing its frame, markers on top. |
| `two_column` | `left`, `right`, `aside` | Two columns of elements, read left then right. |
| `grid` | `cell`, `aside` | Equal elements in a grid of cells. |
| `stacked_list` | `row`, `aside` | Elements stacked top to bottom as rows. |
| `centered_focus` | `center`, `around`, `aside` | One focus element in the middle, the rest smaller around it. |
| `pipeline` | `source`, `stage`, `sink`, `aside` | Stages in flow order (top-down or left-right): sources, middle stages, sinks. |
| `cycle` | `ring`, `center`, `aside` | Steps on a ring that loops back to the start, an optional element in the middle. |
| `swimlane` | `lane-1`, `lane-2`, `lane-3`, `lane-4`, `message`, `aside` | Vertical lanes, one per actor, with ordered messages between them. |
| `versus_split` | `left`, `right`, `shared` | Two halves side by side for the same situation; shared elements span both. |
| `near_far` | `origin`, `near`, `far`, `aside` | An origin with a near and a far destination, the distance drawn to scale. |
| `hub_spoke` | `hub`, `spoke`, `aside` | One hub in the middle with spokes around it. |

## Assets

Asset ids for props that take one (`asset`, `icon`, `role`, `mover`), by family. Ids are exhaustive: there are no others. An unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported as a missing asset. Logo slots declared by the video (`logo_<name>`) may be used like asset ids; never invent one.
